propositions: Rebar currently signs attestations (plan-review, completion-verifier verdicts) with symmetric HMAC; authorship signing and operation certificates require asymmetric signatures verifiable offline by third parties without duplicating security-critical code.
DSSE envelope with PAE must be implemented to sign opaque bytes without re-serialization, eliminating JSON canonicalization and JWT algorithm-confusion attacks per RFC 8725.

SSHSIG scheme via ssh-keygen -Y must sign and verify offline using existing SSH keys with fail-closed behavior on tampered bytes, wrong namespace, unknown principal, substituted key, and expired validity window.
Per-kind policy table (kind → {scheme, namespace, trust-root}) must be pinned out-of-band; the verifier must never select scheme from in-band record data to prevent algorithm confusion.
Existing HMAC-signed attestations must continue verifying after the substrate implementation by registering HMAC as a legacy scheme (regression test requirement).
The signing substrate must have no new core runtime dependencies beyond stdlib; ssh-keygen availability (>= 8.9) must be detected with clear error on absence.
